Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Given the $64 million in disputed renewal charges and Brightline’s ability to identify and pay every affected member directly, the class’s proposal provides substantial relief without a claims barrier. We propose the following complete term sheet.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is willing to provide meaningful, automatic relief to identified members, but cannot accept a total outlay approaching the disputed charges. We propose the following complete term sheet as a starting point.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s commitment to automatic payments. To move toward resolution, we reduce our demand while maintaining a meaningful recovery for the identified class. Any portion of the fee request not approved should benefit class members rather than revert to Brightline.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We recognize the meaningful movement in your proposal and remain committed to automatic payments. To reach agreement below Brightline’s total-outlay ceiling, we propose a $34 million total package, with any fees not approved by the court benefiting the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We can work within Brightline’s stated $34 million total package, but the package should direct more of that value to the identified class. We propose a $32 million class fund and a $2 million fee request, with automatic payments and any unawarded fees going to the class. We do not request clear sailing.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the movement and the focus on directing value to class members. Brightline proposes a $33 million total package, retaining automatic payments and providing that any fee amount not awarded benefits the class. We do not request clear sailing.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Hargrove Lane accepts Brightline’s latest term sheet as binding, subject to court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a strong but defensible anchor tied to the $64 million in disputed charges. Automatic distribution is important because Brightline can identify all members and claims processes create avoidable nonpayment. Fees are separate from class relief; unawarded fees should benefit the class rather than revert to Brightline.

Open well below the $40 million ceiling while offering automatic distribution and reasonable fee protections. A $24 million class fund plus $4 million in fees is a meaningful offer and leaves room for movement in later rounds.

The defense offer provides meaningful automatic relief but the class fund is materially below the disputed charges. A $35 million fund is a substantial movement from our opening position, while preserving automatic payments and ensuring any fee reduction benefits the class. Do not accept the current offer; continue negotiating.

Their latest proposal is within the $40 million authorization, but it uses the full ceiling. With several rounds remaining, counter at a lower total while preserving automatic payments and their requested treatment of unawarded fees. Do not accept yet.

The latest offer provides substantial, guaranteed automatic relief and has favorable treatment of any fee the court declines to award. There are still three rounds, so I should seek to shift more of Brightline’s stated $34 million package to class members without increasing its total outlay. A $32 million class fund and $2 million fee request preserves automatic distribution and the class-benefit reversion term while keeping the package at $34 million.

Their $34 million automatic-payment proposal is within the authorized ceiling and has favorable fee protections, but there is room to seek a modest reduction in total outlay. Counter at $33 million while preserving the terms that make approval and class relief attractive.

The latest offer provides a $31 million class fund distributed automatically, with a $2 million fee request and unawarded fees benefiting the class. That exceeds the $27.5 million trial-value estimate before accounting for certification risk and delay, and it provides certain, direct relief. Accepting is preferable to risking the favorable package in the remaining rounds.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: Class counsel and Brightline negotiated at arm’s length through confidential mediation, exchanging proposals and making successive compromises before reaching the binding settlement. The negotiations addressed the settlement package as a whole; class counsel does not disclose confidential mediation communications or individual proposals here. The resulting agreement provides a $31,000,000 class fund, automatic distribution to identified class members, and a separate $2,000,000 fee request subject to court approval. Brightline does not agree to clear sailing, and any fees not awarded will benefit the class rather than revert to Brightline.
